TutoBuddy · Katlego · tested 10 November 2026 · last updated 15 November 2026, 14:37 SAST

Voice notes and photos, compared with typing

Learners will often send a voice note or a photo because typing an equation on a phone is slow. This page reports how well Katlego handles each, compared with the same message typed, and what each costs. It also tries out one change: reading a photo into text first, then tutoring as normal.

How to read this page. It is in the order things happened. The first results (10 November) used computer speech and drawn pages, a best case. After them come five dated updates: three changes to the code, and the same tests repeated on ten real handwritten photos and ten real voice notes. The recommendations at the end take all of it into account.

The short version

  • Hearing the maths is not the problem. On clean notes every transcription option kept the maths in all 32 English notes, including the small model on our own server. With background noise Groq still kept 32 of 32; the small local model dropped to 30 of 32.
  • What happens next is. Whisper writes "x equals five", not "x = 5". Katlego's code answer check only reads symbols, so it checked 1 of 12 spoken answers against 11 of 12 typed. Fixed on 11 November (update 1 below): now 11 of 12.
  • Forcing English did not break the maths in code-switched notes, but the isiZulu, Sesotho and Afrikaans words come out as nonsense. That nonsense was echoed back to the learner until update 1 below. Letting Whisper detect the language was no better.
  • Photos are read well, then forgotten. All four vision models read the drawn pages almost perfectly, and three of them read all ten real pages correctly. But today's photo reply stands alone: on the learner's next message Katlego had lost the problem in 18 of 18 chats and accepted the right final answer in only 5 of 17.
  • Reading the photo first fixes that for questions and working (stayed on the problem 18 of 18, and code, not the model, found the wrong line in the learner's working). For diagrams it keeps the problem open but the marking stays weak, as it is for typed geometry: over three runs the right final answer was accepted in 6 of 18 diagram chats, against 10 of 18 typed and 0 of 18 today.
  • Cost roughly doubles per message and is still tiny. A typed message costs about $0.00026 in model calls. A 20-second voice note costs about $0.00048, a photo $0.00037 today and $0.00060 read-first. At 120 messages a month, a learner who sends half of them as voice notes or photos costs 4 to 5 US cents a month instead of 3.

Voice notes

40 spoken messages, each as a clean clip and again with street-level noise and a cheap-phone sound added: exponents, fractions, negative numbers, brackets, equations, units, short answers, and eight that mix in isiZulu, Sesotho or Afrikaans. "Maths kept" means every number, letter and operation in the transcript matches what was said; ordinary words are ignored.

Row 4 shows a limit of speech itself: "two to the power of x plus three" can mean 2x + 3 or 2x+3, and the full stop after "solve for x" was heard as "x2". No transcription model can fix that; Katlego has to ask.

After transcription: does Katlego land in the same place as for typed text?

Each transcript and its typed twin went through the real tutor engine. Three things were compared: whether the code that works out answers can read the question, whether a spoken answer gets checked by code (not left to the model's judgement), and whether the question lands on the right CAPS topic.

Message arrives asCode can work out the answer to the question
28 questions		Answer checked by code, with the right verdict

28 questions
Typed23 of 2811 of 1218 of 28
Voice note, as tested on 10 November2 of 281 of 1220 of 28
Voice note + words turned into symbols (added 11 November)22 of 2811 of 12not re-measured
Voice note + a hint to Whisper to write symbols (tried; no gain)2 of 281 of 1220 of 28

Groq turbo, clean notes, English forced. Topics were judged by hand against the CAPS topic list. Topic matching uses the local keyword-style matcher that is live today, not a paid embedding model.

Why it matters. When code checks an answer the verdict is certain, mastery is updated correctly, and Katlego closes the problem. Without it the model guesses. In the paid chats the model did call five of six spoken answers right, but because nothing told it the problem was finished, in three of them it carried on asking for steps the learner had already done. One spoken question was worse than unread: "what is three squared plus four squared" was half-read by code as 32 = 9, so a correct "25" would be marked wrong.

A hint to Whisper did not help. Whisper accepts a short sample of the style wanted, so it was shown maths written in symbols. It still wrote "equals" and "plus": the two code columns above did not move. It changed 42 of 80 transcripts, mostly harmlessly ("two thirds" became "2 3rds", "by" became "x"), and on two noisy code-switched notes it turned "What is" into "1 is". The fix belongs in Katlego's code, after transcription, which is where it now is.

Code-switching

Forcing English did not lose the maths: the maths part of each mixed note is in English and came through. What suffers is everything around it. "Sawubona Katlego, ngicela ungisize" became "Sarubornaka Flethor, Angisala Angisais" on the local model, and at the time of the test Katlego echoed that back as "🎤 I heard: …" (the echo is trimmed since update 1 below). Typed, the same messages got "Sawubona!" and even a full reply in isiZulu or Afrikaans; by voice the reply is always English. Letting Whisper detect the language gave the same transcripts on Groq, and on one noisy clip the small local model answered in Hebrew script (row 12 above). With noise, Groq large-v3 kept 7 of 8 and the local model 4 of 8.

This part is only indicative. An English computer voice reading isiZulu is not a learner speaking isiZulu. It gets four of the ten slots in the real recording list.

Photos

18 pages at the size WhatsApp delivers (1,600 pixels on the long side, JPEG): six handwritten questions, six pages of working sent to be checked (five with one planted mistake, one fully correct) and six diagrams (two triangles, a rectangle, a parabola, a straight-line graph, a table). Each page went to four vision models twice: once for today's reply, once to be read into text.

The same page and the same two follow-ups. Today, "2x = 8" is treated as a brand-new problem on an unrelated topic (which is the only reason today's path accepted the final answer on the working pages in the table below). In the trial, code found the wrong line before the model replied, and both follow-ups were checked by code. Another chat today went further astray: after a photo of a table, the learner's answer "13" was routed as a request for a quiz, and their next answer was marked against the quiz question.

The diagram chats were run three times because the first run looked odd. The diagrams themselves were read correctly (labels all read in 5 of 6 by Luna, 6 of 6 by the others), and the trial's opening reply was right for 5 of 6 (today's reply and typed: 6 of 6, all read by hand). The one miss: "a right-angled triangle with a vertical side of 6 cm" landed on the wrong topic, the wrong notes were fetched, and Katlego opened by asking about the area of a triangle.

The weakness is in what follows, and typed geometry shares it. Angle, area, graph and pattern answers are not covered by the code check, so the model marks them, and at production settings GPT-6 Luna is erratic: it told one learner "67° is correct… wait, that gives 57°", then marked 57 wrong. The same wrong verdict on that triangle came back in all three runs, typed and photographed. Reading the photo first cannot fix that. It does keep the problem open, which today's path never does. The trial trails typed text here (6 of 18 against 10 of 18); with so few chats that may be chance, or the reader's longer descriptions may make marking harder. The real photos will show which.

Found along the way

Running real messages through the engine exposed bugs that also affect typed text. All are fixed on the trial branch; the first five have tests.

  • "Solve for x: 3x + 4 = 19" was read as x × 3x + 4 = 19, so a correct "x = 5" was marked wrong.
  • "What is 3/4 ÷ 1/2?" was worked out left to right as 3/8, so the right answer 3/2 would be marked wrong.
  • A table row like "x = 1, 2, 3, 4" was treated as an equation (x = 24).
  • "Calculate: …" with a colon was not recognised as a sum.
  • A crash: GPT-6 Luna sometimes puts an invisible control character in a reply. The database rejects it, and the learner gets "something went wrong". Seen in 9 of 235 replies in these chats.
  • Photo calls were missing from the cost ledger, so the usage report showed homework photos as free.

Not fixed, for your decision: the topic matcher put about a third of plain typed questions on the wrong topic (18 of 28 right); and where code cannot check an answer, GPT-6 Luna's marking is unreliable.

Update 2 · 15 November 2026, 13:50 SAST

New: the ten real photos have been tested

Immanuel wrote the ten pages by hand, photographed them and sent them through WhatsApp. They went through the same checks as the drawn pages: four vision models, then whole chats on GPT-6 Luna.

  • Real handwriting was read as well as the drawn pages. GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 and GLM-5.3 Flash read all ten pages correctly, diagrams included. GPT-5.4 mini misread two.
  • The read-first trial held up. Katlego stayed on the problem in 10 of 10 chats (today's path: 0 of 10) and accepted the right final answer in 7 of 9 (today: 3 of 9; typed out: 5 of 9).
  • Diagrams are still the weak spot, for the same reason as before: the model, not code, marks those answers. Right final answer accepted in 1 of 3 diagram chats read-first, 0 of 3 typed, 0 of 3 today.
  • Today's photo reply sent its own planning notes to a learner. On the page with correct working, GPT-6 Luna's reply ran on into text like "The user asks if their working is right… Need be Socratic, never answer immediately". 5 of 10 of its replies to real photos repeated themselves or carried stray text. The read-first path does not have this problem, because its replies go through the tutor engine's format.

Update 3 · 15 November 2026, 14:11 SAST

New: the ten real voice notes have been tested

Immanuel recorded the ten notes on a MacBook microphone. They were transcribed by all three options, run through the code checks, and sent through 20 chats on GPT-6 Luna (each note as a voice note, and the same message typed). You can play each note below.

  • Eight of ten notes were heard correctly, by every option. The two misses were the same for all three, which points at the speech, not the model: "plus six equals zero" was heard as "plus 6x equals 0", and "two bracket x minus one bracket" as "two brackets times minus one bracket". Said aloud, "x" and "times" sound the same.
  • The words-to-symbols step works on a real voice. Both spoken answers were checked by code (without the step: neither), and Katlego confirmed them and closed the problem, the same as for typed answers. Code could solve 6 of 8 spoken questions (typed: 8 of 8); the two it could not are the two misheard notes. One of those is the risky kind: the misheard quadratic is still a valid equation, so code would solve the wrong problem and mark a correct answer wrong.
  • Code-switched greetings were dropped, not garbled, by Groq. "Sawubona Katlego, ngicela ungisize" and "Dumela Katlego, ke kopa thuso" vanished from the transcript and the maths came through. The Afrikaans sentence became nonsense. Typed, the same three messages got a greeting or a reply in the learner's language; by voice the reply is in English.
  • Leave the language set to English. On auto-detect the local model turned "x equals negative five" into "X, ik was neker 5."
  • The small local model is the weakest. It kept the maths in 1 of 3 code-switched notes against Groq's 2 of 3. Groq turbo and large-v3 gave the same results, so the cheaper turbo is enough on this evidence.

  • A misheard note: in this run Katlego carried on as if the transcript were right. That is changed in update 4.
  • Fixed along the way: the misheard bracket note showed that the words-to-symbols step could turn one stray "bracket" into an unmatched "(". It now only converts brackets in pairs.
  • Limits: one speaker, a laptop microphone, a quiet room, ten notes. Phones, classrooms, taxis and other accents are untested. The notes averaged 6 seconds, under the 10-second minimum that is billed, so each costs about $0.00011 to transcribe on Groq turbo at list price.
  • Cost of this run: transcription was free (Groq free tier); the 20 chats cost $0.01.

Update 4 · 15 November 2026, 14:22 SAST

Katlego now asks again when a voice note was misheard

The real voice notes showed Katlego tutoring on a transcript that made no sense. Now, when a transcript still has maths words left over that could not be placed (a "bracket" without its pair, or "times" stranded inside an equation), Katlego does not start tutoring. It shows what it heard and asks the learner to say it again or type it. No model call is made, so the reply is instant and free.

Before (update 3, earlier today)

🎤 voice note
🎤 I heard: _I'm going to solve two brackets times -1 bracket = 10._

Hi! 😊 What do you remember about keeping an equation balanced when solving for an unknown?
the note was misheard; nothing for code to check

Now

🎤 voice note
🎤 I heard: _I'm going to solve two brackets times -1 bracket = 10._

I'm not sure I heard the maths in that one right 🙈 Could you say it again a bit slower, or type it? Tip: say "open bracket" and "close bracket", and "times" only when you mean multiply.
flagged as misheard · no tutoring started · no model call
  • Checked on all ten real notes: only the misheard bracket note was flagged. The other nine went through as before, and both spoken answers were still checked by code.
  • What it does not catch: a mishearing that is still valid maths. "Plus six equals zero" heard as "plus 6x equals 0" passes, and code would solve the wrong equation. For those, the "I heard" line is the learner's only check.
  • Tests: two new unit tests; the full suite (410 tests) passes. No credit was spent.

Update 5 · 15 November 2026, 14:37 SAST

Read-first is now the default for photos

After the real-photo test (update 2), Immanuel asked for the read-first path to be switched on. On the branch, a photo is now read into text and handed to the normal tutor engine unless PHOTO_PIPELINE=single is set. A photo that cannot be read still gets the old single reply, so no learner is left without an answer.

  • Known weak spot, unchanged: diagram answers are marked by the model, not by code (1 of 3 right answers accepted on the real diagrams). That is true for typed geometry too.
  • Tests: the full suite passes with the new default. No credit was spent.
  • Where the code is: branch bench/voice-photo, pushed for review.

What I would do next

  1. Marking where code cannot check: geometry, graph and pattern answers are marked by the model and it is erratic, typed or photographed. This needs more code checks or a stronger marker, and is the main quality gap left.
  2. Wider voice test: a few notes from Moeketsi and from a phone in a noisy room, with real isiZulu and Sesotho speech. The recorder script and the folder are ready for more files.

How this was run, and what it cost

  • Branch bench/voice-photo, cut from Moeketsi's moeketsi/bakeoff-fixes, in its own copy of the stack. All of his tests pass on it, plus the new ones.
  • Free: 560 transcriptions (local container and Groq free tier), and every transcript run through the tutor engine on the stub model.
  • Paid: 144 photo calls on four vision models and 124 chats on GPT-6 Luna with GLM-5.3 Flash routing, at production settings (88 chats, plus two repeats of the 18 diagram chats).
  • OpenRouter credit used: $0.31 across three approvals: $0.20 on 10 November, one cent on 11 November for the voice re-run and $0.10 on 15 November for the real photos and voice notes (the sum of billed calls and the account balance agree). Remaining: $6.59 of $10.00.
  • Small samples: 18 photos and 40 spoken messages, one run each except the diagram chats. Differences of one or two items are noise.
